chunks: And young attendants like pearls within their shells, will go round.

key_terms.غِلْمَانٌ: Young attendants or servants in Paradise
key_terms.لُؤْلُؤٌ: Pearls, used as a metaphor for beauty and purity
key_terms.مَكْنُونٌ: Hidden or preserved, indicating they are kept pure from defects

ai.seo_question: Who are the ghilman mentioned in Surah Al-Waqi'ah and what does 'lu'lu'un makhun' mean?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'hidden pearls' (lu'lu'un maknun) symbolize the ghilman whose perfection is concealed from the eyes of the general public, reserved exclusively for the purified believers, reflecting the concept of 'Ismah (infallibility) and inner purity. This imagery underscores the divine preservation of these servants from minor defects, serving as a metaphor for the spiritual refinement awaiting the faithful in Jannah.
